synopsis: South Africa is the only jurisdiction the booklet found with a legal mandate for automatic slow-down and braking on heavy mining machines; the relevant regulations were published on 27 February 2015 and commenced on 21 December 2022 without a transitional period, after suspension because suitable technology was unavailable [f164, f1363, f10724, f11457]. For diesel-powered trackless mobile machinery, the rules require detection and warning, slowing to a safe speed and automatic braking if the operator does not act, plus failure to a safe state without human intervention [f2079, f2080]. The law preceded validation standards and specifies no detection percentage, distance, false-alarm limit or stopping-distance test; subsequent industry specifications supply quantitative criteria, including a 200 m minimum detection range and emergency-stop deceleration of 1.9 m/s² above 20 km/h or 1.0 m/s² for other machines [f1360, f2081, f11458, f2113, f5560]. Independent verification milestones include the surface TMM test specification dated 29 August 2025, the verification regime dated 11 October 2025 and the TRL7 stage-gate specification dated 20 January 2026, but the corpus identifies no prescribed allowance for virtual testing [f555, f556, f557, f1249]. The immediate Level 9 mandate pushed deployment before refinement, while a trade report suggesting December 2023 conflicts with the documented December 2022 commencement [f358, f359, f11461, f1364, f1363]. Safety outcomes remain a concern rather than proof of mandate effectiveness: total mining fatalities fell from 55 in 2023 to 42 in 2024, but trackless-mobile-machinery fatalities rose from six to nine [f3138, f3140].
